answer_1.quote: In coherent PMD, it must additionally generate a rationale R = (Q, A), where Q = {Q 1 , Q 2 , . . . , Q n } and A = {A 1 , A 2 , . . . , A n } are respectively sequences of n yes-no questions and their predicted answers... We prompt the VLM to generate a series of questions... After a question is generated, it is answered by the VLM
answer_1.outputs: Sequences of yes-no questions and answers forming rationales for procedural mistake detection

answer_2.quote: We calculate two evaluation metrics for coherent PMD: relevance of questions and informativeness of answers... We implement f e with BART fine-tuned on the large-scale MultiNLI dataset... Rel(Q′|T, Q, A) = |p_e(T|Q, A ∪ {(Q′, Yes)}) − p_e(T|Q, A ∪ {(Q′, No)})|

answer_4.quote: To validate these metrics... we performed a small human annotation study... We recruited 5 annotators... to rate the relevance and informativeness of 10 machine-generated questions... Annotators were instructed to rate how relevant the potential next question is... on a scale from 1-5
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated relevance on a 1-5 scale (very irrelevant to very relevant) and informativeness on a 1-5 scale (very uninformative to very informative) following specific instructions about task context and decision criteria
